_comment: Vehicle and boat manufacturers (scripts/sim/manufacturers.gd), for Vehicles companies. Each maker's vehicles are their own market good (its id is the commodity id, added to data/markets.json's at load by GameData): unit is a vehicle (cars and trucks, carried by the car carriers) or a boat (carried by the boat carriers); hold is how many deck slots one takes (a ship's capacity is in slots: a superyacht takes 60); its base price is value_per_slot[line] x class_value[class] x hold. Prices: cheapest (factory_price) at the maker's factories, home_price over its home region, and elsewhere what that class sells for there (demand[class] by the region's wealth: luxury most expensive where people are rich, budget where they aren't), evened out over the map like every good. class: budget, mainstream, premium or luxury; size: how many factories it has (small 1, mid 2, large 3). kind: the cargo art it shows on deck (cars, trucks, boats). rivals: makers of the same kind and class (direct competitors). Likeness (0-100, start) is each company's standing with each maker: trading its goods (buying them, and more, selling them) raises it by gain x sqrt(value / gain_ref_value) x (taper_from - likeness) / 100, and lowers its rivals' by rival_penalty of that; a ship that breaks down with its goods aboard costs breakdown_penalty, one lost lost_penalty. perks: likeness at which its own factories sell to the company buy_discount cheaper (cheaper_at), its buying there no longer pushes their price up (first_pick_at), it may build a factory for the maker (factory_at) and a second (second_factory_at). A factory goes at any port where the maker has none (its own or any company's) in a region the company has unlocked: it costs factory_cost[class] to build and upkeep_a_month of that a calendar month (paid a day at a time), makes output_slots_a_month deck slots of the maker's vehicles a month into the company's stockpile there (up to stock_months of output), which it sells there or its ships load free; the maker takes cut_high of what they sell for at factory_at likeness, falling to cut_low at 100. Closing a factory, the maker buys it back for close_share of what it cost.

makers.name: Hoshino Motors
makers.blurb: Nagoya's giant: sensible saloons and hatchbacks by the million, with a plant in South Carolina for the American market.

makers.name: Kaminari
makers.blurb: A few thousand screaming sports cars a year from a workshop outside Osaka, each signed by the engineer who built its engine.

makers.name: Daebak Auto
makers.blurb: Busan's value champion, building cheerful compacts at home and in Chennai for half the world's first-time buyers.

makers.name: Seonghwa
makers.blurb: Quietly superb executive cars from Incheon, with a newer plant at Qingdao chasing China's managers.

makers.name: Longwei Motors
makers.blurb: The world's cheapest new cars, rolling out of three vast plants by the shipload for emerging markets everywhere.

makers.name: Jinxing EV
makers.blurb: Shenzhen's battery-car upstart: sleek electric saloons with screens where the dashboard used to be.

makers.name: Rheinwerk
makers.blurb: German engineering by the trainload through Bremerhaven, and a Georgia plant building SUVs for America.

makers.name: Adlerhof
makers.blurb: Long, silent limousines for chauffeurs and heads of state, built in Hamburg and finished in Antwerp.

makers.name: Velloro
makers.blurb: Twelve cylinders, scissor doors and a waiting list: Genoa's red supercars go out a few at a time, crated.

makers.name: Corsetti
makers.blurb: Tiny, stylish city cars from Rome and Tangier, made for narrow streets and tight parking.

makers.name: Marchand
makers.blurb: Comfortable French family cars and people carriers from Le Havre, and a Valencia plant for the south.

makers.name: Albion Motor Company
makers.blurb: Walnut, leather and a bonnet as long as a cricket pitch: grand tourers hand-built near Southampton since 1921.

makers.name: Lakeshore Motors
makers.blurb: Detroit's old guard: full-size pickups and big comfortable saloons, from Michigan, Ohio and a plant at Veracruz.

makers.name: Pioneer Trucks
makers.blurb: Chrome-stacked long-haul tractors and delivery lorries from Chicago and Houston.

makers.name: Nordvik Trucks
makers.blurb: Gothenburg's indestructible heavy trucks and coaches, with a Brazilian plant at Santos for the Americas.

makers.name: Sagar Motors
makers.blurb: India's people's carmaker: tough little hatchbacks built in Mundra, Chennai and Kolkata for crowded roads.

makers.name: Garuda Trucks
makers.blurb: Workhorse light trucks for the islands' farms and building sites, from Jakarta and Surabaya.

makers.name: Pampa Motores
makers.blurb: Flex-fuel compacts and little pickups for South America's roads, from Santos and Buenos Aires.

makers.name: Southern Cross Motors
makers.blurb: Big-hearted V8 saloons and utes built for the outback, from Melbourne and Adelaide.

makers.name: Amur Trucks
makers.blurb: Six-wheel-drive trucks from Vladivostok that will cross a frozen river or a swamp, and start at forty below.

makers.name: Desert Falcon
makers.blurb: Gold-trimmed, armoured luxury SUVs from Dubai, for sheikhs, celebrities and anyone with something to fear.

makers.name: Savanna Motors
makers.blurb: Durban's tough bakkies and simple small cars, made to last on Africa's roughest roads.

makers.name: Lazzaro Yachts
makers.blurb: Sixty-metre superyachts with helipads and beach clubs, launched at La Spezia and fitted out in Genoa.

makers.name: Vanderhaven
makers.blurb: Dutch steel superyachts built to cross any ocean, a handful a year from the Rotterdam yards.

makers.name: Elbwerft
makers.blurb: Sleek, dark-hulled motor yachts from a Hamburg yard on the Elbe, engineered like a watch.

makers.name: Solent Marine
makers.blurb: Fast, glamorous sports yachts from the Solent, a favourite of film villains and footballers.

makers.name: Gulf Pearl Yachts
makers.blurb: Gleaming white motor yachts built in Dubai for the Gulf's marinas and the Riviera's.

makers.name: Mistral Voiliers
makers.blurb: Bluewater cruising yachts from Marseille and Valencia, the boat half the world's sailors dream of retiring on.

makers.name: Tasman Cats
makers.blurb: Racing-bred sailing catamarans from Auckland, fast enough to win the big races and roomy enough to live on.

makers.name: Formosa Yachts
makers.blurb: Solid teak-trimmed trawler yachts from Kaohsiung, built for long slow passages and loved by liveaboards.

makers.name: Muskoka Classics
makers.blurb: Gleaming mahogany runabouts hand-built near Toronto, the classic boat of every lakeside cottage.

makers.name: Cape Craft
makers.blurb: Cape Town's sturdy charter catamarans, sailed off to the Caribbean and the islands by the hundred.

makers.name: Bluewater Boatworks
makers.blurb: Florida's centre-console sportfishing boats, with rod holders, live wells and a lot of outboard.

makers.name: Gulfstream Marine
makers.blurb: America's favourite family bowriders and pontoon boats, from Houston, Mobile and a Great Lakes plant at Detroit.

makers.name: Wavecrest
makers.blurb: Aussie aluminium and fibreglass trailer boats for fishing the reef and the bays, from Brisbane and Sydney.

makers.name: Yamakaze Marine
makers.blurb: Jet skis and little outboard runabouts by the hundred thousand, from Osaka, Nagoya and Miami.

makers.name: Fjordline Båt
makers.blurb: Sturdy Norwegian day cruisers with a cabin and a heater, built for the fjords' cold summers.

makers.name: Baltic Sails
makers.blurb: Affordable cruising sailboats from Gdańsk and Helsinki, the charter fleets' workhorse.

makers.name: Rio Náutica
makers.blurb: Bright, fast speedboats from Rio and Santos, built for the beaches and the samba weekends.

makers.name: Lakeland Boats
makers.blurb: Tough riveted aluminium fishing boats from Milwaukee and Duluth, sold at every bait shop in the North.

makers.name: Nanhai Boats
makers.blurb: Dinghies, tenders and small fibreglass boats by the container load, from three yards on China's coast.

makers.name: Malabar Boatyards
makers.blurb: Fibreglass fishing boats for the coasts of India and Africa, from Kochi and Mundra.

makers.name: Aegean Caiques
makers.blurb: Painted wooden caiques built the old way near Piraeus, for fishermen and island tavernas.

makers.name: Andaman Marine
makers.blurb: Longtail boats and simple skiffs from Port Klang, the water taxis of Southeast Asia's coasts.
